bib.title: A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores
bib.venue: Proceedings of the Third Conference on Machine Translation (WMT), Volume 1: Research Papers

question: How much do undisclosed BLEU parameters and reference preprocessing change reported scores, and how should MT papers report BLEU so scores are comparable?
hypothesis: User-supplied reference tokenization is the main cause of incomparable BLEU scores across papers.
contributions: Quantifies BLEU variation from reference tokenization and case on WMT'17
Shows influential papers' BLEU configurations are often not recoverable
Proposes metric-internal (WMT 13a) reference processing as the standard
Releases SacreBLEU, which downloads references and emits a version string

method.summary: Scores a single WMT'17 system (online-B) and its references under four tokenization schemes, cased and uncased, per language arc, and tabulates the spread. Audits seven well-cited papers for which BLEU configuration they used, and releases SacreBLEU.

datasets.name: WMT 2017 news test sets (en<->cs, de, fi, lv, ru, tr)
datasets.preprocessing: basic: Moses tokenizer; split: compound splitting; unk: words under 2 occurrences in WMT training target side mapped to UNK; metric: mteval-v13a.pl internal tokenization

datasets.name: WMT14 en-de
datasets.size: 2,737 sentences (evaluation release) vs 3,004 sentences (post-evaluation full release)

inference.samples: one system output per arc, one score per configuration; no repeats

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: corpus-level n-gram precision metric (max n-gram 4 virtually always), with length penalty, smoothing for zero counts, number of references as parameters

eval.protocol: range row = largest minus smallest score across configurations, excluding unk; cased and lowercased (lc) variants

availability.data: SacreBLEU downloads WMT 2008-2018 and IWSLT 2017 test sets
